mountains.name: Everest
mountains.description: The highest summit above sea level, rising on the Himalayan crest between Nepal and Tibet.

difficulty.rationale: Extreme altitude, glacier travel and exposed climbing.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Aconcagua
mountains.description: A towering Andean peak in Mendoza, Aconcagua is the highest mountain in the Americas.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Denali
mountains.description: North America’s highest mountain rises above Alaska’s glaciers, with a vast snowy massif and two main summits.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Kilimanjaro

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Elbrus
mountains.description: A twin-summited volcano in the Caucasus, Elbrus is the European peak in the Seven Summits collection.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Vinson
mountains.description: Antarctica’s highest mountain rises in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains, surrounded by immense ice fields.

difficulty.rationale: Remote Antarctic glacier travel, expedition logistics and extreme cold.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Carstensz Pyramid
mountains.description: Also known as Puncak Jaya, this limestone peak in New Guinea is the highest mountain in Oceania.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: K2
mountains.description: The world’s second-highest mountain is a dramatic pyramid in the Karakoram, on the Pakistan–China border.

mountains.name: Kangchenjunga

mountains.name: Lhotse

mountains.name: Makalu

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Cho Oyu
mountains.description: This broad Himalayan summit stands west of Everest along the Nepal–Tibet border.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Dhaulagiri I

mountains.name: Manaslu
mountains.description: Manaslu rises in Nepal’s Mansiri Himal, its snowy ridges overlooking valleys of the Gorkha region.

mountains.name: Annapurna I
mountains.description: The highest peak of the Annapurna massif, Annapurna I was the first eight-thousander to be climbed.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Gasherbrum I

mountains.name: Broad Peak

mountains.name: Gasherbrum II
mountains.description: A snowy Karakoram pyramid in the Gasherbrum group, close to Gasherbrum I and Broad Peak.

difficulty.rationale: Remote glacier travel and climbing at extreme altitude.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Shishapangma
mountains.description: The lowest of the classic fourteen eight-thousanders, Shishapangma stands entirely within Tibet.

mountains.name: Mount Fuji

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Mont Blanc

mountains.name: Eiger
mountains.description: This Bernese Alps peak is famous for its immense north face above the village of Grindelwald.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Rainier
mountains.description: Also known as Tahoma, this glacier-covered volcano dominates the skyline of Washington’s Cascade Range.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Whitney
mountains.description: The highest summit in the contiguous United States rises among the granite peaks of California’s Sierra Nevada.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Aoraki / Mount Cook
mountains.description: New Zealand’s highest mountain rises in the Southern Alps, surrounded by glaciers and sharply cut alpine ridges.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Kinabalu
mountains.description: A granite massif in Sabah, Mount Kinabalu rises above Borneo’s tropical forests. Its highest summit is Low’s Peak.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Rinjani

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Bromo
mountains.description: This active volcano sits inside the broad Tengger caldera, surrounded by a volcanic plain known as the Sea of Sand.

difficulty.ascent: Established crater viewpoint path and stairs, when open
difficulty.rationale: A comparatively short approach and staircase; access depends on volcanic restrictions.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Fansipan
mountains.description: Vietnam’s highest mountain rises in the Hoàng Liên Sơn range near Sa Pa.

difficulty.ascent: Tram Ton trekking ascent, excluding the cable car
difficulty.rationale: A sustained mountain trek with steep ground and substantial elevation gain.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Olympus
mountains.description: Greece’s highest mountain is a multi-peaked massif associated with the gods of ancient Greek mythology. Its highest summit is Mytikas.

difficulty.ascent: Final scrambling ascent to Mytikas in dry summer conditions
difficulty.rationale: Exposed scrambling to the highest summit, beyond the walking routes to lower peaks.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Toubkal
mountains.description: North Africa’s highest mountain rises in Morocco’s High Atlas, south of Marrakesh.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Kenya
mountains.description: An ancient volcanic massif near the equator, Mount Kenya has jagged summits and high alpine valleys. Batian is its highest point.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Damavand
mountains.description: Iran’s highest mountain is a prominent volcanic cone in the Alborz range, northeast of Tehran.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Ararat
mountains.description: A large volcanic massif in eastern Türkiye, Mount Ararat consists of Greater Ararat and the smaller Little Ararat.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Fitz Roy
mountains.description: Also called Cerro Chaltén, this dramatic granite peak rises above Patagonia near the town of El Chaltén.

tripLength.context: Typical expedition itinerary including approach, acclimatization and weather allowance; international travel excluded.

mountains.name: Mount Kosciuszko

difficulty.rationale: A maintained walking route; winter snow changes the demands substantially.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Ben Nevis

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Table Mountain

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Machu Picchu

difficulty.ascent: Inca Trail trek to the archaeological site
difficulty.rationale: Stone stairways and sustained trekking over high passes; the site elevation is lower than the trek’s high point.

tripLength.context: Classic Inca Trail itinerary to the citadel; excludes travel to the trailhead and prior acclimatization. A direct site visit is much shorter.

mountains.name: Huayna Picchu
mountains.description: The distinctive steep peak rising behind the terraces of Machu Picchu.

difficulty.ascent: Permitted summit trail from Machu Picchu
difficulty.rationale: Very steep stone steps and exposed sections require sure footing.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Pico de Orizaba

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Iztaccíhuatl
mountains.description: A sprawling volcanic ridge whose profile inspired the name Sleeping Woman.

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Nevado de Toluca

tripLength.context: Typical route itinerary; international travel and any prior acclimatization excluded.

mountains.name: Alpamayo

mountains.name: Mount Batur
